title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 3.53 (versions follow prime numbers; 353 after 349): her letters as vectors of particles, at full resolution. Each learned letter (16 x 16 dots from her book of letters) is told as straight strokes, each time the one covering the most ink not yet covered; drawn at any size, each stroke lets out its particles along it (Bresenham), like an SVG. She now hands the kernel a screen twice as big (1280 x 698), shown dot for dot without touching the kernel; what she drew stays as it was, and her text panel is drawn in fine dots. Each letter is drawn by the finest telling she has that the surface can show; one she only knew coarse (the digits) she learns once from her book of letters. Measured in a copy of her house: no more processor than before (40 s against 52 s for the same talk, within the noise). Stated: forms, creatures and her music are still 2 x 2 blocks, and strokes are straight. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v3.53: letras de partículas, a resolución completa. Prototipo de investigación.
